newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply higher on late buying.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply higher on late buying.

text.p: Waves of strong, late buying in profit-backed plastics pulled Taiwan's stock index to a sharply higher close on Monday and brokers said the index would test strong resistance at 7,000 points in the near term.
The index shot up 156.75 points or 2.30 percent to end at 6,982.81. Turnover was an active T$77.78 billion.
Late buying focused on stocks related to the Formosa group, one of Taiwan's biggest and most influential conglomerates, driving the market to yet another 22-month closing high.
"Buying emerged all of a sudden and everybody as asking why," said Oliver Fang, analyst at National Securities.

The late buying suggested market fearlessness despite new strains in the island's ties with China, brokers said. In a new shock, Taipei's biggest diplomatic ally South Africa, said on November 27 it would switch recognition to Beijing in 1997.
The index fell after Pretoria's move but recovered despite Taipei's countermeasure -- freezing China economic initiatives.
"Gains today showed that most investors have confidence in big-capital, profit-backed companies," Fang added.

Key Formosa member Nan Ya Plastics was the second most active issue, jumping the daily seven percent limit to end at T$69. Formosa Taffeta and Formosa Plastics both soared to end limit up at T$33.7 and T$73 respectively.

"We can see the market structure is quite healthy. It did fall on the news of South Africa's diplomatic switch, but it came back quickly and sentiment remains good," said Lin Long-hsien of United Securities. Current loose liquidity and an expected fourth-quarter recovery were big positives, he said.
